incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: Elevated kv-cache churn + continuous-batching backlog detected for model redwood-phi-1 (us-west). Paging oncall.
Sam: I'm oncall, looking now. Any customer flags yet?
Mira: CS says two enterprise tenants seeing intermittent 502/504s and huge token-level latency spikes on long-chat sessions. P99 token latency up ~3x for some flows.
Ash: Observing batch depth steadily climbing; batch sizes spike to ~512. KV cache key churn high — many speculative drafts creating short-lived keys, eviction thrash. Memory usage on node set A creeping up.
Jake: Logs show speculative-decoder spawning many candidate drafts that never resolve; each draft touches kv-cache entries with distinct prefix keys. This interacts badly with continuous batching because a bunch of tiny drafts get grouped into huge batches.
Leah: Customer impact: AcmeCorp and Nimbus.ai both reported production errors at ~15:12 UTC, affecting ~1.2% of requests but concentrated on long-history chat routes. CS prepping templated notice.
oncall: Handoff: Sam taking lead, Mira shadowing, Ash on runtime changes, Jake on telemetry and traces. See playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/kvcache-spec-decode (internal)
Sam: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) slow speculative decoding 2) cap batch size 3) enable temporary kv eviction guardrail 4) rate-limit offending routes.
Ash: Quick config patch I can push to canary nodes to limit batch_max_size and batch_timeout. Applying to canary first.

Ash: Pushing config now to canary via infra API:

```json
{"batch_max_size":128,"batch_timeout_ms":15,"speculative_max_concurrent":4}
```

Mira: Can we disable speculative for the model entirely while we triage? That would stop draft churn immediately.
Sam: Let's not blanket disable yet — try conservative throttle first on canary. If we still see blowups, then disable.

Jake: Telemetry after config push (canary): batch depth down from 512 -> 96, kv-miss churn rate down ~70%, memory growth stabilized. P99 token latency on canary flows trending down.
Leah: CS: drafting customer message, will hold until we confirm mitigation working.

Sam: Rolling the change to 20% of serving fleet now. Watch for regressions (short-lived throughput dip expected).

Ash: Noted one side-effect: a rolling restart of canary pods triggered transient 5xx for ~30s. Increased healthcheck grace on next rollout.

Jake: Adding a temporary per-model guard in routing layer to prevent batching mixing drafts and targets from different sessions. Quick patch:

```diff
- allow_cross_session_batching = true
+ allow_cross_session_batching = false
```

Mira: After 40m of gradual rollout to 20% -> 60% -> 90%, error rate normalized and token P99 returned near baseline. On the 90% step we saw one spike when old config pods still receiving traffic; rolled back that subset.

Sam: Decision: Keep speculative enabled but with stricter heuristics: only prefetch when kv_cache.hit_rate >= 0.75 and limit speculative_max_concurrent=4. Also keep batch_max_size=128, batch_timeout_ms=15 for next 2 hours.

Ash: I'll open a quick hotfix PR to make these defaults safer and add tests for speculative + continuous-batching interplay. PR: https://git.redwood/hotfixes/patch-kr-442 (internal)

Leah: Customer comms: sending initial notice noting mitigation and that we're monitoring; offering meeting if they see further issues. Template: "We're aware of intermittent errors on long chat sessions, mitigations applied, monitoring in progress. We'll follow up with root cause." :slightly_smiling_face:

Sam: Follow-ups for postmortem:
- root cause hypothesis: speculative-decoder created high cardinality KV keys for draft tokens while continuous-batching aggregated these across sessions, leading to eviction thrash and large batches that spiked memory and latency.
- action items: add guardrails in speculative decoder, add batch mixing safeguards, add canary healthhooks to block large batch rollouts, telemetry alert for kv-churn spikes.

Ash: Quick note: applied a transient TTL cap on per-prefix entries to reduce eviction pressure while we stabilize. Config snippet: 

```yaml
kv_cache:
  eviction_policy: LRU
  per_prefix_ttl_ms: 120000  # 2 minutes during mitigation
```

Jake: Monitoring set: 4h watch, alert if kv-churn or batch_depth > 300. Also recording traces for example failing requests for the postmortem.

Mira: Oncall handoff at 18:00 UTC to night shift. Sam will document state and handover.

Sam: Handing off — system stable on current mitigations, rolling to full fleet paused until hotfix PR merges and QA passes. Attaching notes to incident doc.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied; partial rollback to safer defaults performed. Incident moved to "monitoring".

Leah: CS sent customer notice. No major data loss; only increased latency and transient 5xx. Customers responded appreciating the rapid response.

Ash: Post-incident follow-ups: scheduler test to simulate speculative+batch combo, safety gate for batch size increases, add integration test to avoid high kv-key cardinality from speculative drafts.

Jake: Saving traces and logs to incident archive: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2234001234/archive

Sam: Closing thread — marking for postmortem write-up tomorrow. Thanks team. :heart:

incident-bot: RESOLVED: Monitoring period started, will auto-close in 4h if stable.
